questions.stem: Which of the following best defines an audit trail?
options: A record allowing every figure in the accounts to be traced back to the transaction and user that created it
The route an auditor takes through the company's premises
The list of documents an auditor must sign
The order in which the financial statements are prepared
questions.why: A trail records the date, user and reference for each posting, which supports internal control and deters fraud.
whyNot: It is a data record, not a physical route.
Signing documents is not what a trail is.
That is the order of preparation, unrelated to the trail.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines what-if analysis?
options: Changing one input in a model to see the effect on the result
Comparing actual results with the budget
Checking a spreadsheet for formula errors
Preparing several budgets for different departments
questions.why: Spreadsheets recalculate automatically, which makes sensitivity testing practical in a way manual working does not.
whyNot: That is variance analysis.
That is error checking.
That is departmental budgeting.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines an integrated accounting package?
options: Software in which entering a transaction once updates all the related ledgers and reports
Software that combines accounting with word processing
Software used by more than one company
Software that prepares only the financial statements
questions.why: Integration removes duplicate keying and means the ledgers cannot disagree with each other, because there is only one set of data.
whyNot: Integration refers to the accounting modules, not to office software.
Shared use by companies is not what integration means.
An integrated package covers invoicing, payroll, inventory and the ledgers.

questions.stem: What does EPOS stand for and do?
options: Electronic point of sale: it records each sale and updates the inventory records at the same time
Electronic purchase order system: it places orders with suppliers automatically
Electronic payroll operating system: it calculates wages and deductions
Electronic profit and overhead statement: it allocates overheads to products
questions.why: EPOS links the till to the inventory records in real time, which supports reordering and sales analysis.
whyNot: Automatic reordering can follow from EPOS but is not what the term means.
Payroll is a separate module.
That is not a recognised term.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the specific weakness of spreadsheets for accounting records?
options: They have almost no built-in controls or audit trail, so an error produces a confident wrong answer
They cannot perform arithmetic accurately
They cannot be used for budgeting
They can only be used by one person at a time
questions.why: A formula copied to the wrong range or a hard-coded number typed over a formula produces no warning at all.
whyNot: The arithmetic itself is reliable; the model may not be.
Budgeting is one of their main accounting uses.
Files can be shared, though version control is then a problem.

questions.stem: Why do spreadsheets suit cash budgeting particularly well?
options: A cash budget is a chain of dependent calculations, so changing one input recalculates every month instantly
A cash budget contains no formulas
Cash budgets are required to be prepared in spreadsheet form
Spreadsheets automatically exclude depreciation
questions.why: That is what makes sensitivity analysis practical: the effect of a delayed receipt or a later purchase appears immediately.
whyNot: A cash budget is almost entirely formulas.
There is no such requirement.
The user must exclude depreciation; the software does not know to.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a financial advantage of computerised accounting?
options: Faster invoicing, which improves cash flow
The removal of all need for training
The elimination of input errors
Guaranteed compatibility with every other system
questions.why: Faster invoicing and instant ageing analysis both improve cash collection, and routine posting costs fall.
whyNot: Training is one of the main costs of implementation.
Input errors remain; only calculation errors are removed.
Compatibility is a technical risk that must be managed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a financial disadvantage of computerised accounting?
options: High initial costs of hardware, software, licences and training, which a small business may not recover
Slower production of management reports
Loss of the ability to produce invoices
Higher labour costs for routine posting
questions.why: For a business with few transactions the savings may simply not justify the cost, which is the sharpest evaluative point in this topic.
whyNot: Reports are produced faster, not more slowly.
Invoicing is one of the main functions gained.
Routine posting costs generally fall.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a technical risk of computerised accounting?
options: Dependence on the system, so a failure can halt the accounting function or trading itself
The inability to handle large volumes of transactions
The need to recalculate every figure by hand
The impossibility of backing up data
questions.why: With EPOS a failure can stop trading altogether, and data loss, corruption and security threats are real risks.
whyNot: Handling volume is one of the main advantages.
Calculation is automatic.
Automatic backup is one of the advantages, though backups do fail.

questions.stem: What does garbage in, garbage out mean in this context?
options: The system calculates faithfully whatever it is given, so wrong input produces wrong output
The system deletes data that is entered incorrectly
Old data must be removed before new data is entered
The system cannot process unusual transactions
questions.why: The output arrives quickly and with an unjustified appearance of authority, which makes the consequence of poor input larger, not smaller.
whyNot: The system does not detect or delete incorrect data.
That is data housekeeping, not the principle.
Unusual transactions can normally be recorded.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a human disadvantage of introducing a new accounting system?
options: Resistance to change from staff who fear the system or the loss of their role
The removal of tedious routine work
Improved employability from new skills
Easier reading of reports by non-specialists
questions.why: Retraining costs time and money, some staff will not adapt, and job losses damage the morale of those who remain.
whyNot: That is an advantage.
That is an advantage.
That is an advantage.

questions.stem: Why is an audit trail only as good as the system's controls?
options: If users share a single login, actions cannot be attributed to anyone
Audit trails are only kept for one month
Auditors are not permitted to examine electronic records
A trail cannot record the date of a posting
questions.why: Attribution is what makes the trail useful for control and deterrence, and shared access destroys it.
whyNot: Retention is a matter of configuration, not a fixed limit.
Electronic records are routinely examined.
A trail records the date, user and reference.

questions.stem: Why can errors be more damaging in a computerised system than a manual one?
options: One wrong setting is applied consistently to thousands of transactions
Errors cannot be corrected once entered
Computerised systems make more arithmetic errors
Errors are never visible in the output
questions.why: The speed and consistency that are the system's strength also propagate a single mistake at scale.
whyNot: Errors can be corrected, ideally with the correction recorded.
Arithmetic is more reliable, not less.
Errors do appear in the output, which is the problem.

questions.stem: What is a limitation of EPOS for inventory control?
options: The records show what should be there, so a physical count is still needed
It cannot record the value of each sale
It cannot identify slow-moving lines
It cannot be linked to reordering
questions.why: Mis-scanning and theft distort the records, so comparing the count with the system is how stock loss becomes visible.
whyNot: Recording the value of each sale is one of its core functions.
Identifying slow and fast movers is one of its main benefits.
Automatic reordering at a reorder level is a standard feature.

questions.stem: In which situation is investing in ICT for accounting least likely to be worthwhile?
options: A very small business with few transactions and staff who cannot easily be retrained
A business with several sites and a large inventory of many lines
A growing business whose manual systems are already straining
A business needing frequent management information
questions.why: The benefit depends on transaction volume, which is the single most useful condition to state in an evaluation.
whyNot: Multiple sites and many inventory lines make the case strongest.
Growth straining the manual system is a clear argument for investing.
Frequent reporting needs are a strong argument for investing.

questions.stem: Why might an unreliable power or internet supply be a legitimate argument against heavy ICT dependence?
options: A system failure can halt both accounting and trading, so dependence becomes an operational risk
Accounting software cannot be installed without permanent internet access
Electronic records are not legally valid in such locations
Power failures corrupt all backups automatically
questions.why: For island and remote operations this is a real consideration rather than an excuse, and it belongs under technical aspects.
whyNot: Many packages run locally without constant connectivity.
Electronic records are legally acceptable.
Backups are not automatically corrupted, though the risk of data loss rises.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of an integrated package over separate records?
options: Entering a transaction once updates all the related ledgers, so they cannot disagree
It removes the need for any accounting knowledge
It guarantees the business will be profitable
It eliminates the need for an audit
questions.why: Single entry removes duplicate keying and the errors that come with it.
whyNot: Interpretation and judgement still require accounting knowledge.
Software does not affect profitability directly.
An audit is still required where the law requires one.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a use of accounting software named in the specification?
options: Producing invoices, a receivables list, payroll and tax returns
Designing the company's products
Negotiating with suppliers
Recruiting and selecting new employees
questions.why: Those are the functions the specification lists, alongside spreadsheets for budgeting and EPOS for inventory control.
whyNot: Product design is not an accounting function.
Negotiation is a purchasing activity.
Recruitment is a human resources activity.

questions.stem: Will you be examined on the use of specific software packages?
options: No: the specification states that specific applications and packages are not examined
Yes: you must know one named package in detail
Yes: you must compare at least two named packages
Only in Section A of the paper
questions.why: The specification says candidates will not be examined on the use of specific applications or software packages, so answers should be about uses and effects.
whyNot: No package is prescribed.
No comparison of named packages is required.
The exclusion applies to the whole paper.

questions.stem: What is the most balanced overall judgement on ICT in accounting?
options: It changes the nature of the work rather than removing the need for judgement, while making poor data and weak controls more costly
It removes the need for accountants entirely
It has no effect on the quality of accounting information
It is always worthwhile whatever the size of the business
questions.why: Staff move from posting to interpreting, and the consequences of bad input, weak controls and misplaced confidence become larger and quicker.
whyNot: Interpretation, judgement and scepticism remain essential.
It affects speed, accuracy and availability of information substantially.
For a very small business the cost may exceed the benefit.

questions.stem: Which four headings does the specification use for the advantages and disadvantages of ICT?
options: Audit trail, financial, technical and human
Cost, quality, speed and accuracy
Planning, control, coordination and motivation
Materials, labour, overhead and capital
questions.why: Using these four as the paragraphs of a written answer guarantees breadth and follows the mark scheme's structure.
whyNot: Those are general performance measures, not the specified headings.
Those are the purposes of budgeting.
Those are cost classifications.
